And if it is a Paschal offering that is not
With regard to which halakha … to eat them in their blemished … These

With regard to which halakha would the possibility that it is a firstborn or animal tithe need to be taken into account? It is with regard to the halakha that one is permitted to eat them in their blemished state, as firstborns and animal tithes do not need to be redeemed if they develop a blemish, but are eaten as such. But perhaps it is a sin-offering, … a sin-offering … in its first year, … and … an … in its second year was found.

But perhaps it is a sin-offering, as it is permitted to bring a female sin-offering? The Gemara answers: The animal for a sin-offering is always in its first year, and the mishna is referring to a case where an animal in its second year was found.
